title: Post-deploy runbook gaps and hotfix log — Nov 2025
content:
SUMMARY:
Quick catch-up from the field this week after three on-prem/VPC rollouts. Primary theme: small, recurring post-deploy friction points that are adding ~15–60m of manual work per site and a customer-facing latency regression at one install. This doc captures the incidents, root hypotheses, immediate hotfixes we shipped, and concrete runbook / tooling gaps to close before the next wave.

ATTENDEES:
- Owen Brooks (owner)
- Aisha Patel (network lead)
- Claire Zhang (observability)
- Diego Martinez (deploy field engineer)
- Lina Kovac (SRE on-call)

CONTEXT / WHAT HAPPENED THIS WEEK:
1) AtlasPay (customer X) — warm traffic latency spike after initial warmup (~1.5x p95 for 30m). Symptoms: token generation p95 and tail memory spikes on gpu-node-3 during KV cache priming. Customers observed intermittent ~300–600ms extra tail latency.
2) BetaRetail — SNAT port exhaustion surfaced after we enabled external metrics collector; outbound telemetry bursts caused ephemeral connection churn and NAT port reuse errors on customer border appliance.
3) EdgeSite-7 — two manual reboots after post-deploy systemd race on service start where redis-init occasionally timed out and proxy started before kv-cache mounted.

INCIDENT NOTES / EVIDENCE:
- AtlasPay: tracing shows repeated cache misses on prefix cache for initial user cohort; eviction heuristics aggressively compacted first-come keys when batch size spiked. Slow path observed when fallback model variant was fetched over the network.
- BetaRetail: iptables/NAT logs show ephemeral port reuse; customer firewall metrics spiked in close temporal correlation with our telemetry export bursts.
- EdgeSite-7: journalctl shows redis-init exit 124 followed by proxy startup event — race window ~7s.

HOTFIXES / MITIGATIONS APPLIED (timeline):
- 2025-11-02 09:10 UTC: AtlasPay — temporarily pinned model-variant to local quantized copy and disabled aggressive cache compaction (patch pushed to 1.3.2-hotfix). Result: p95 returned to baseline within 12 minutes.
- 2025-11-03 02:45 UTC: BetaRetail — rate-limited telemetry exporter (burst 20/s, sustained 2/s) and added client-side random jitter to metrics flush. Customer confirmed NAT error counts dropped to near-zero.
- 2025-11-04 16:30 UTC: EdgeSite-7 — reordered systemd unit dependencies and added a simple start-retry loop for redis-init; deployed as 1.3.2-bootpatch.

ROOT HYPOTHESES / OBSERVATIONS:
- Runbook gap: no standardized preflight for customer border NAT capacity or telemetry export cadence. We rely on heuristics but not explicit checks.
- Cache behavior: current default eviction policy is tuned for cost (compact aggressively) not for warmup latency; this can hurt initial p95 during bursty onboarding.
- Start ordering: some installs with slower NVMe or NFS mounts expose race windows not encountered in QA because QA images are slightly faster.
- Monitoring blindspot: KV-cache miss-rate and per-node eviction logs are not part of default telemetry shipped to hosted console for private deployments — we were blind until customer traces arrived.

ACTION ITEMS (owners + due dates):
- A1. Add "border-NAT capacity" checklist item to preflight with explicit sample commands and expected thresholds; owner: Aisha P.; due: 2025-11-10.
- A2. Introduce a temporary warmup profile toggle that biases eviction toward retention for first 30 minutes post-deploy; implement config + doc; owner: Diego M.; due: 2025-11-12.
- A3. Instrument per-node KV-cache metrics (misses, evictions, compaction events) and add them to default telemetry bundle for private installs; owner: Claire Z.; due: 2025-11-14.
- A4. Add start-order watchdog in systemd unit that enforces redis-init completion or does graceful backoff; owner: Lina K.; due: 2025-11-09.
- A5. Draft a short runbook appendix for common firewall/NAT issues with sample iptables netstat commands and interpretation; owner: Owen B.; due: 2025-11-08.

RISKS / OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Will the warmup retention profile increase steady-state memory/cost on tiny dedicated pools? Need load modeling (ask optimize team).
- Some customers use corporate load balancers that NAT across multiple internal hosts — do our heuristics handle port re-use patterns at scale?
- Can we auto-detect vulnerable start-order sites by measuring disk mount latency during preflight and fail fast?

NOTES TO SELF / WORKING THOUGHTS:
- Consider a 'deploy sanity' CI step that simulates first-100-requests warmup and emits a tiny synthetic trace; could catch eviction mis-tuning earlier.
- Short-term toggle OK, but long-term we should teach eviction to be workload-aware (duration-based retention policy).
- Telemetry bundle bloating: prioritize compact counters + event sampling rather than full traces for private installs by default.

FOLLOW-UPS / NEXT MEETINGS:
- Quick sync Friday 2025-11-07 09:00 PT to triage progress on A1–A4. Invitees: Aisha, Diego, Claire, Lina, Owen.
- Postmortem doc (internal) to be drafted after A2 experiment closes — owner: Owen. Target: 2025-11-20.

EXTRA CONTEXT / LINKS (for handoff):
- AtlasPay support thread: SUP-3191
- Related engineering tickets: ENG-4382 (eviction policy refactor), ENG-4470 (start-order watchdog)
- Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Post-deploy+Runbook

END NOTES:
This felt like a classic "assumed network and storage homogeneity" problem. We solved customer-visible pain with small hotfixes; next priority is to make those fixes standard and automated so ships are low-friction. Keep the fixes small and observable — no big risky refactors in the hot path.

-- Owen
